events.title: Dutch West India Company Chartered
events.description: The Dutch West India Company received its charter from the States General of the Dutch Republic, granting it a monopoly on trade in the Americas and West Africa.
events.significance: The company played a central role in Dutch colonial expansion, including the founding of New Amsterdam (later New York), and in the Atlantic slave trade.

events.title: Publication of 'Casey at the Bat'
events.description: Ernest Thayer's poem 'Casey at the Bat' was published in the San Francisco Examiner.
events.significance: The poem became one of the most famous works of American baseball literature and a lasting piece of American popular culture.

events.title: Edward VIII Marries Wallis Simpson
events.description: The Duke of Windsor, formerly King Edward VIII, married American socialite Wallis Simpson in France, after abdicating the British throne in December 1936.
events.significance: The abdication and marriage triggered a constitutional crisis and brought George VI to the throne, shaping the modern British monarchy.

events.title: Ed White Performs First American Spacewalk
events.description: Astronaut Ed White spent about 20 minutes outside the Gemini 4 spacecraft, becoming the first American to walk in space.
events.significance: The spacewalk was a key step toward the Apollo moon landings, demonstrating that astronauts could work outside a spacecraft.

events.title: Tiananmen Square Crackdown Begins
events.description: Chinese troops and tanks moved into central Beijing on the night of June 3-4 to clear pro-democracy protesters from Tiananmen Square.
events.significance: The crackdown ended weeks of demonstrations, killed many civilians, and remains a defining and heavily censored event in modern Chinese history.
